limitations: A single automated GET is not proof that an API is unavailable and must never be used on its own to remove a README entry.
No API keys, tokens or authenticated calls were used.
The assigned README URLs are landing/documentation pages; no documented API endpoint was called.
CORS was not inferred from the fact that a browser can open a URL.

Every 2xx HTML response body, direct or redirected, is inspected up to 32768 bytes to look for an explicit login form; a body read timeout is reported as TIMEOUT and a body read error as CONNECTION_ERROR.
A login form beyond that 32768-byte inspection prefix may not be seen; non-HTML and 204/205 bodies are not inspected.

DNS resolution uses one lookup per hop with a bounded caller wait. The underlying resolver call cannot be cancelled; a late result is ignored, and the connection uses only the addresses already validated from that lookup.
TCP connection attempts across the validated addresses share one connect deadline. There are no request retries.
Redirect following is limited to 5 redirects and 6 requests per URL.
HTTP, DNS, TLS and bot-protection behaviour is a point-in-time observation and can vary by network, geography and CDN.
AUTH_WALL includes HTTP 401/403 and login/identity-provider redirects; it is not evidence that an API has disappeared.
